title: The Gopatha Brahmana
attributionNote: Anonymous priestly prose of the Atharvaveda tradition, named after the sage Gopatha and transmitted without an author's name.
description: The Gopatha Brahmana is the only Brahmana of the Atharvaveda: it explains the sacrificial formulas of that Veda, the duties of the brahman priest who supervises the rite, the ceremonies of the year, the anointing of a king, and the verses by which each offering is understood. Its two parts move from the order of the sacrifice to the Veda itself and the persons who may keep it.
historicalContext: The Atharvaveda had no Brahmana of its own in the older series, and the Gopatha was composed late to supply the lack; it is therefore a Brahmana written after the period of the Brahmanas, and its account of the Veda and its reciters is read as evidence for how the corpus was understood in the last centuries before the common era.
availabilityNote: Complete: both prapathakas and 5,242 units of the GRETIL e-text, which follows Arlo Griffiths's transcription, streamed at read time one anuvaka at a time. The file's opening colophon, which it numbers 0.0.0, is dropped.
